comparison: Both address EPCAM as a marker for pancreatic epithelium (C15-C21, C83-C84). OpenEval finds the claims well-supported by immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, and RT-qPCR data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising critical concerns about the 45% of EPCAM+ cells with low PDX1/NKX6-1 levels, questioning what these cells represent and requesting integration with previous work. Major disagreement on completeness of characterization.

Both evaluate GP2+ multipotent progenitor claims (C1, C27-C32, C88). OpenEval finds claims supported by flow cytometry and transcriptomic data, though notes uncertainty about true multipotency (C89). Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, noting decreased novelty due to authors' 2017 paper and requesting clarification on whether GP2+ represents truly multipotent cells or lineage-committed progenitors. Both identify the multipotency question as requiring additional evidence.

Partial overlap on GP2 population characterization (C25-C26). OpenEval supports the consistent inter-individual frequencies. Peer reviewers request more complete data presentation (GP2/ECAD staining for all populations) and more quantitative summaries with statistical comparisons, indicating incomplete data presentation.

Both address acinar differentiation (C2, C37, C39). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and transcriptomic comparison with adult pancreas. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED without challenging the acinar findings. Strong agreement on this aspect.

Both evaluate NEUROG3 expression and endocrine differentiation sequence (C3, C42-C44, C59-C61, C94). OpenEval finds claims well-supported by RT-qPCR and flow cytometry showing sequential marker changes. Peer reviewers also rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the temporal sequence documentation, though requesting additional analysis of other endocrine cell types beyond beta cells. General agreement with minor extension requests.

Both address temporal marker expression and endocrine maturation (C4, C46-C55). OpenEval finds claims supported by flow cytometry showing sequential changes, noting inference of differentiation progression is reasonable but direct lineage tracing would be stronger. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the temporal progression model without challenge. Strong agreement.

Minimal overlap on GP2- population heterogeneity (C45). OpenEval addresses CD142/SUSD2 subsets within this population. Peer reviewers support the heterogeneity interpretation based on marker expression data. Agreement on this limited aspect.

Both evaluate single-cell RT-qPCR data on endocrine progenitor subsets (C57-C58, C62-C68). OpenEval finds claims supported by data on 172 and 166 cells showing marker enrichment, noting limitations of single timepoint analysis. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, raising critical questions about whether two distinct beta cell populations were identified and requesting analysis of other hormone-expressing cells (GCG, polyhormonal) not provided in the study. Disagreement on interpretation completeness.

Both address transcriptomic analysis and comparison with adult data (C33-C36, C38, C41). OpenEval finds claims supported by PCA, GSEA, and comparison with adult single-cell RNAseq, noting some detection power limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting substantial improvements: unclear gene enrichment cut-offs, missing supplementary tables, undescribed correlation methods, limited heatmap gene selection, inclusion of additional datasets, and specific questions about PAX4 expression. Major disagreement on analytical rigor and completeness.

Both evaluate hPSC-derived cell comparison with fetal pancreas (C5, C69-C74, C106). OpenEval finds claims supported by side-by-side comparison showing similar marker patterns across three cell lines, noting validation is limited to marker expression without functional assessment. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on which cell lines were used for which experiments and noting hPSC-derived cells display fetal rather than adult phenotypes. Both identify limitations but peer reviewers emphasize insufficient experimental details.

Both address ductal lineage characterization (C40). OpenEval finds claim supported but notes ductal lineage receives less detailed characterization than other lineages. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the GP2- population heterogeneity interpretation. Agreement that data supports claims but characterization is limited.

Both address methodological and ethical documentation (C108-C110). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate documentation of ethical compliance and tissue procurement. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning precision of developmental timing, requesting clarification on biological vs technical replicates, suggesting supplementary table for tissue samples, and noting methods are only superficially described. Disagreement on adequacy of methodological documentation.

OpenEval evaluates claims about PDX1/NKX6-1 low progenitors (C85-C86) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of functional validation or lineage tracing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these claims, though R1 touches on related heterogeneity concerns.

OpenEval addresses uncertainty about GP2+ population composition and multipotency (C89), appropriately acknowledging lack of single-cell lineage tracing. No separate peer review result specifically addresses this claim, though it is discussed within R2's evaluation of multipotency claims.

OpenEval evaluates ECAD expression patterns and temporal regulation (C92-C93, C96) as SUPPORTED based on flow cytometry data, noting functional role is inferred rather than tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates inference of lineage progression from temporal data (C99) as SUPPORTED but notes it is based on population-level analysis rather than direct lineage tracing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates NEUROG3+ cell heterogeneity across SUSD2 subsets (C104) as SUPPORTED by single-cell RT-qPCR, noting it refines previous reports. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates the methodological advance of functional enrichment in sorted populations (C105) as SUPPORTED, noting limitations in antibody availability and functional assays. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background/context claims (C6-C14, C22-C23, C75-C82, C87, C90-C91, C95, C97-C98, C100-C103, C107) as SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations, noting these provide context but are not novel findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found as these are established knowledge.
